blocks.text: Why you need Excel for data governance analysts on mac

Data governance is about policy, but it is also about hands on data work. You need a tool that handles quick lookups and format changes without overhead. Excel on macOS is that tool. It is reliable for small to medium datasets. You can use it to verify data quality before it enters your master catalog. It is not a database, but it works for quick audits.
Common Excel tasks for data governance

items: Mapping data lineage across different source files.
Validating data formats like phone numbers or IDs.
Comparing two versions of a data dictionary.
Flagging blank cells in critical metadata columns.
Creating quick pivot tables to identify data outliers.

blocks.text: Practical tips for your Mac workflow

Your Mac is a powerful tool for governance. Use Spotlight by pressing ⌘ + Space to open your files instantly. If you have too many windows, use Mission Control to see everything. For Excel specifically, ensure you use the correct shortcuts. Avoid using the mouse for simple tasks. Press ⌃ + Space to select a column. Press ⇧ + Space to select a row. These small habits add up over a long day.

Excel has a limit of 1,048,576 rows. If your data exceeds this, it will truncate. Always check your row counts before importing. Use the Filter feature by pressing ⌘ + ⇧ + L. This helps you isolate specific data quality issues. If you need to remove duplicates, use the Data tab in the ribbon. It is under Data Tools > Remove Duplicates. It is a simple way to clean your metadata entries.

Documenting lineage is often manual. Keep a master sheet with columns for Source, Transformation, and Destination. Use Data Validation to create drop down lists. Go to Data > Data Tools > Data Validation. This ensures your team uses consistent terms. It reduces noise in your governance reports. If you need help with a specific menu, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where it is.

Excel is not for everything. If you are doing complex lineage mapping, use a dedicated catalog tool. Tools like Alation or Collibra are better for enterprise scale. Use Excel for the quick tasks. Use your catalog tool for the permanent record. This keeps your process clean and audit ready.

items: Do not store sensitive PII in local spreadsheets.
Always back up your work to a secure cloud drive.
Use absolute references with $ signs to prevent formula errors.
Check your data types after importing CSV files.
Do not rely on hidden rows for data security.

faq.question: Can Excel handle large data governance files?
faq.answer: Excel supports up to 1,048,576 rows. If your data is larger, use a database or a specialized tool.
